texts: Before a redo CABG in a patient with a patent LIMA to the LAD, the work-up is a CT scan with contrast, an echocardiogram and an assessment of the conduits still available.
The CT shows how close the patent LIMA, the heart and the aorta lie to the back of the sternum, so re-entry can be planned and the LIMA protected.
The echo assesses ventricular and valve function, and the conduit study (veins, radial arteries) shows what grafts are left.
Injury to a patent LIMA at re-entry causes a large anterior infarction and is a leading cause of death in redo surgery.
FFR or intravascular ultrasound of the left main adds nothing here, because the stenosis is already clearly significant.
In the picture, Chopper's map marks the cat's slice showing the vine behind the stern, the bat, and Usopp measuring the spare conduits.
Memory hook: before sawing an old stern, map the vine behind it.
